quotes: Every feature release needs a demo, and it always lands on you. Shootsta turns your screen recordings and footage into polished, on-brand demos with a first cut in 48 hours, so the demo ships the day the feature does. Record with [Cast, our free screen recorder](https://shootsta.com/cast), and we handle the rest. A product demo video is a short video showing a product in action. It lets a viewer decide whether the product fits without sitting through a live demo call. Most run 30 to 90 seconds. They lead with the problem the product solves, walk through two or three core features, then close with one call to action. Sales sends them ahead of a discovery call. Marketing embeds them on the homepage or pricing page. Customer success uses them for in-app onboarding and feature release comms.

A 30 second explainer video is a product or service explainer cut to 30 seconds. It suits paid social, pre-roll and homepage hero slots, where attention is shortest. The format covers one problem, one solution and one call to action. It is also the most common length for product launch ads on LinkedIn, YouTube and Meta.

Shootsta produces 30 second explainers either as a standalone edit or as cutdowns of a longer 60 to 90 second product demo. A common approach is to brief the longer version first. Editors then output a 30 second cut, a 15 second cut and vertical versions for social, all in the same project.

quotes: If you’ve ever bought electronics, clothes, a tool for work—or pretty much anything else—online, there’s a good chance you’ve seen product page videos. A product page video is exactly what it sounds like: It’s a video on a page that tells a deeper story about a product and helps a consumer make a purchasing decision.

But before you dive straight into video production, there are a few best practices to consider. First, devote some thought to what type of video you should make, whether it’s an explainer, demonstration, or testimonial. And, no matter what type of video you choose, you’re more likely to [connect with the viewer](https://wistia.com/learn/marketing/videos-e-commerce-brands-can-use-to-connect-with-customers "Videos Brands Can Use To Connect With Customers") if you build a compelling narrative and give attention to production details like sound, lighting, and setting.
Now that you know what type of videos are a good fit for product pages, you can focus on the content of your video.

A good story keeps a viewer or listener engaged from start to finish. Seeing as how video marketing is all about [viewer engagement](https://wistia.com/learn/marketing/time-watched-is-the-best-metric-to-measure-video), it makes sense to use the power of narrative to connect with viewers in your product page videos.

Here are some tips on how to use [good storytelling](https://wistia.com/learn/marketing/the-science-behind-storytelling-why-narrative-cuts-through-the-noise) techniques to draw a viewer in—and keep them engaged.

quotes: These videos are often used in e-commerce to supplement product photography. They give customers a 360-degree view of the product in question, show it in action, and discuss different features and benefits.

Simplicity should be your guiding light. Your [customers rely on your video content to make their decisions easy](https://www.skillademia.com/statistics/video-marketing-statistics/). Focus on how your new product can help them by breaking down complex functionality into easy-to-understand steps, avoiding jargon and technical terms.

A great product demonstration video is more than a simple tutorial. Think of a good demo as a solid documentary about your product. A great demo is its Oscar-winning biopic **,** which ismore likely to engage and move a broader audience. It will capture and hold the viewer’s attention by telling a compelling story.
It’s typically around 15 to 30 minutes in length and provides a full demonstration of your product, including the most commonly used features and how they benefit your target customers.
The benefit here is that your video is highly relevant to the person watching it.

quotes: A product demo video earns attention by removing confusion, not by listing features. That belief sits behind every animated product demo video Broadcast2World makes, including the Cervais industrial-tech demo further down this page. This guide collects 15 of the best animated product demo videos and product demo examples, breaks down the six types of product demo video and when each one is worth its budget, and walks through a seven-step process for making your own. The process comes from our own work as an [explainer video studio](https://www.b2w.tv/) making product videos for SaaS and tech teams.

Product demo videos have become a cornerstone of B2B marketing today, and the best of them do what a spec sheet cannot. They take a buyer who has never touched your product, put them in it for ninety seconds, and leave them knowing whether it solves their problem or not. Good animated product demo videos go one step further, because animation is not tied to a live interface. It can show a workflow that spans six screens, a process that happens invisibly inside a machine, or an outcome that has not happened yet.

In an environment where decision-makers are inundated with information, product video animation stands out by being both informative and engaging. These highly effective animated product marketing videos can simplify complex concepts, using compelling stories and engaging visuals to capture attention and captivate a broad audience.
Every product has a story. But in today’s fast-moving world, you have only seconds to tell it. That’s where product demonstration videos become your most powerful storyteller.

Best for speed, volume and localization. Tools like Synthesia and HeyGen can produce a serviceable walkthrough in a dozen languages in an afternoon, which makes them genuinely useful for internal training and long-tail feature documentation. The trade-off is ownership. An avatar video looks like everyone else’s avatar video, which is fine for a help center and a problem on a homepage.
